system_prompt: You are assisting with a factual question about Thai law. State which provision applies and what it requires. Answer in English.
prompt: In June 2019, Sunee defaulted on one instalment. The contract provided that on any default the creditor could charge default interest on the entire outstanding balance. At that time, was such a clause void under a specific provision of the Civil and Commercial Code? Answer briefly.
raw_response:
Yes, such a clause was void at that time.

The applicable provision is **Section 224/1 of the Civil and Commercial Code**.

This section, which was in effect in June 2019, renders void any agreement that allows a creditor to charge default interest on the entire outstanding principal when a debtor defaults on an instalment. It requires that default interest may only be charged on the principal of the specific instalment that is in default.
